newsitem.title: UK: British Treasury gets numbers crossed, misfires in cyberspace.
newsitem.headline: British Treasury gets numbers crossed, misfires in cyberspace.

text.p: Britain's Treasury Department misfired in cyberspace Wednesday, releasing an erroneous figure on interest rates on the very day the Bank of England issued a warning on the dangers of conducting business on the Internet.

In its annual report, the Bank of England said it welcomed more choice for customers as institutions offer banking services on the worldwide computer network. But it said cowboys may abuse the system and consumers might not always be able to tell if the institution was authorized, or from where it was operating.

But if caution was the central bank's watchword, it was missed by the finance ministry. When the Treasury released minutes on Wednesday of crucial talks between the finance minister and Bank of England Gov. Eddie George, it muddled its numbers and had to admit the old-fashioned paper version of events was the one to be trusted.
"The printed version shows (George) asked for a quarter point rise and that is correct," said a Treasury spokesman.

The Internet version said George favored a half-point rise -- much to the shock of some traders since degrees of a percent can amount to millions lost or gained in the hurly-burly of world financial markets.
Said one embarrassed Treasury insider, "Oh no. This is terrible. I'll have to go and kick the machine."
